plan.english: Once there was no night. The Twin and his sister were alone. Then the Twin died, the first of mortals. His sister sat beside the body; she cried and did not eat. Her tears flowed onto the body. The gods said to her: "Forget your brother." She said: "My brother is gone." The sun did not go down, and she did not forget. Then the gods put night between the days. Black night came, and the stars and the moon flashed up. The sister slept. In the morning Dawn grew bright, and the sister forgot her grief. In the night mortals forget grief.

clauses.english: Once there was no night.
The Twin and his sister were alone.
Then the Twin died, the first of mortals.
His sister sat beside the body; she cried and did not eat.
Her tears flowed onto the body.
The gods said to her: "Forget your brother."
She said: "My brother is gone."
The sun did not go down, and she did not forget.
Then the gods put night between the days.
Black night came, and the stars and the moon flashed up.
The sister slept.
In the morning Dawn grew bright, and the sister forgot her grief.
In the night mortals forget grief.

plan.english: The Twin is the first of mortals who died. No one followed him. Below, in the darkness, he sought the path. He crossed the black river by the ford, and the cold current came up to his knees. An eagle flew before him and showed him the ford. On the other side he found a broad pasture. There cows eat sweet grass. In the pasture he sat down and became king of the dead. He found the path for many, the path which our dead went. That path our grandsons will go. A mortal does not flee from death.

clauses.english: The Twin is the first of mortals who died.
No one followed him.
Below, in the darkness, he sought the path.
He crossed the black river by the ford, and the cold current came up to his knees.
An eagle flew before him and showed him the ford.
On the other side he found a broad pasture.
There cows eat sweet grass.
In the pasture he sat down and became king of the dead.
He found the path for many, the path which our dead went.
That path our grandsons will go.
A mortal does not flee from death.

title: The Two Dogs of the Path

plan.english: Two dogs guard the path of the dead. They are the dogs of the Twin. Their eyes are red, and their teeth are white. They walk among men. Whom death has seized, him they seek. They lead him by the path to the king of the dead. Dead one, run past the two dogs! Do not be afraid of them. Throw them grain and honey, and they will let you go. Walk by the good path to the old ones. There may dear ones receive you.

clauses.english: Two dogs guard the path of the dead.
They are the dogs of the Twin.
Their eyes are red, and their teeth are white.
They walk among men.
Whom death has seized, him they seek.
They lead him by the path to the king of the dead.
Dead one, run past the two dogs!
Do not be afraid of them.
Throw them grain and honey, and they will let you go.
Walk by the good path to the old ones.
There may dear ones receive you.

plan.english: Yonder flows a black river. No man swims through it, and no fish lives in it. An old man waits at the ford with a boat. He carries the dead over the water. He takes a wage from the dead, a piece of bronze. He questions each dead man: "Whose son are you?" The dead man says the name of his parent. Then he carries him in the boat. Whoever does not know his own lineage stays here in the cold, crying. So a man teaches his boy his lineage.

clauses.english: Yonder flows a black river.
No man swims through it, and no fish lives in it.
An old man waits at the ford with a boat.
He carries the dead over the water.
He takes a wage from the dead, a piece of bronze.
He questions each dead man: "Whose son are you?"
The dead man says the name of his parent.
Then he carries him in the boat.
Whoever does not know his own lineage stays here in the cold, crying.
So a man teaches his boy his lineage.

plan.english: The Twin and his brother were alone. There was no sea, and there was no sky. Then the brother slew him with a knife. From his flesh he created the earth, and from his bones the stones. From his blood he created the water, and from his eyes the sun. From his head he created the sky, and from his breath the wind. From his mind he created the moon, and from his mouth the fire. The earth is the body of the Twin. When a mortal dies, his bones go to the stones, and his breath flies to the wind.

clauses.english: The Twin and his brother were alone.
There was no sea, and there was no sky.
Then the brother slew him with a knife.
From his flesh he created the earth, and from his bones the stones.
From his blood he created the water, and from his eyes the sun.
From his head he created the sky, and from his breath the wind.
From his mind he created the moon, and from his mouth the fire.
The earth is the body of the Twin.
When a mortal dies, his bones go to the stones, and his breath flies to the wind.

plan.english: Good-Fame sang songs, and the beasts listened. A snake bit his young wife, and she went below. He walked down to the house of the dead. The dogs at the door heard his song and lay down. There he sang before the king of the dead. The dead stood around him and listened. The king heard the song, and his heart grew warm. He said: "Take your wife and lead her to the light. Do not turn around on the path." Good-Fame led his wife up through the darkness. At the light he turned and looked at her. Then she vanished into the shadow. Good-Fame sings alone, and his song is sad. The beasts follow his voice.

clauses.english: Good-Fame sang songs, and the beasts listened.
A snake bit his young wife, and she went below.
He walked down to the house of the dead.
The dogs at the door heard his song and lay down.
There he sang before the king of the dead.
The dead stood around him and listened.
The king heard the song, and his heart grew warm.
He said: "Take your wife and lead her to the light.
Do not turn around on the path."
Good-Fame led his wife up through the darkness.
At the light he turned and looked at her.
Then she vanished into the shadow.
Good-Fame sings alone, and his song is sad.
The beasts follow his voice.

plan.english: Kindly spoke to the young Man-Fame: "Son, two paths stand before you. If you stay at home, you will live a long life, and your name will vanish. If you go to war, you will fall early, and imperishable fame will be yours. Choose!" Man-Fame chose fame. He yoked the swift horses and drove the chariot to war. He slew many enemies, and he fell early at the ford. Kindly cried. In the morning her tears lie on the grass. Now men praise him. The fame of a hero does not die.

clauses.english: Kindly spoke to the young Man-Fame:
"Son, two paths stand before you.
If you stay at home, you will live a long life, and your name will vanish.
If you go to war, you will fall early, and imperishable fame will be yours.
Choose!"
Man-Fame chose fame.
He yoked the swift horses and drove the chariot to war.
He slew many enemies, and he fell early at the ford.
Kindly cried.
In the morning her tears lie on the grass.
Now men praise him.
The fame of a hero does not die.

plan.english: Dawn loved a mortal. She went to Sky, the father, and asked: "Sky, may he be immortal!" Sky gave him an imperishable lifetime. Dawn forgot youth. The husband became old and lay down. He did not die; he lay and spoke, and no one listened. His body dried up, and his voice remained. Dawn hid him in her house. In the morning she leaves him and goes to the sky. Mortals grow old; the gods do not grow old.

clauses.english: Dawn loved a mortal.
She went to Sky, the father, and asked:
"Sky, may he be immortal!"
Sky gave him an imperishable lifetime.
Dawn forgot youth.
The husband became old and lay down.
He did not die; he lay and spoke, and no one listened.
His body dried up, and his voice remained.
Dawn hid him in her house.
In the morning she leaves him and goes to the sky.
Mortals grow old; the gods do not grow old.

plan.english: When a child is born, the Allotter comes to the household. He gives the child its portion. With him sit three women. He stretches out a thread. The women pour milk for the Allotter at the hearth. While the thread is whole, the man lives. When the Allotter cuts off the thread, he falls asleep. No one flees from his own portion. The king is mortal, and the shepherd is mortal. The gods are immortal. Honor the Allotter, and he will give a long thread.

clauses.english: When a child is born, the Allotter comes to the household.
He gives the child its portion.
With him sit three women.
He stretches out a thread.
The women pour milk for the Allotter at the hearth.
While the thread is whole, the man lives.
When the Allotter cuts off the thread, he falls asleep.
No one flees from his own portion.
The king is mortal, and the shepherd is mortal.
The gods are immortal.
Honor the Allotter, and he will give a long thread.

title: The King Who Hid from Death

plan.english: Good-Horses was an old king; he had ruled for many years. Death came to his door. Good-Horses said: "Who is at my door?" "I am Death; I have come." Good-Horses became afraid and hid himself in the darkness. Death sought him and found him. "No one hides from death." She seized his hand and led him to the dark path. His sons laid him into a hollow. They put a cup and a spear beside him and raised a heap of stones. They burned a bull and a goat with fire, and his friends sang his deeds. His name lives in his grandsons.

clauses.english: Good-Horses was an old king; he had ruled for many years.
Death came to his door.
Good-Horses said: "Who is at my door?"
"I am Death; I have come."
Good-Horses became afraid and hid himself in the darkness.
Death sought him and found him.
"No one hides from death."
She seized his hand and led him to the dark path.
His sons laid him into a hollow.
They put a cup and a spear beside him and raised a heap of stones.
They burned a bull and a goat with fire, and his friends sang his deeds.
His name lives in his grandsons.

plan.english: Beloved son, why did you leave me? I bore you, I nourished you, I loved you. You drank milk from my breast. I clothed you in a white garment. Now you lie in the darkness. Your eyes do not look at the sun. Your ears do not hear my words. Who will bring me water when I am old? Death, you seized my child; seize me now! My tears flow.

clauses.english: Beloved son, why did you leave me?
I bore you, I nourished you, I loved you.
You drank milk from my breast.
I clothed you in a white garment.
Now you lie in the darkness.
Your eyes do not look at the sun.
Your ears do not hear my words.
Who will bring me water when I am old?
Death, you seized my child; seize me now!
My tears flow.

plan.english: Husband, you fell early and left me a widow in the house. Our son is young. Who will protect him? Who will protect me? Enemies will come and lead us away. You did not give me your hand; you did not speak a word to me. Your horses stand by the door and wait for you. Your bed is cold. Now I cry, and the women cry with me. Your fame is great, and my grief is great.

clauses.english: Husband, you fell early and left me a widow in the house.
Our son is young.
Who will protect him?
Who will protect me?
Enemies will come and lead us away.
You did not give me your hand; you did not speak a word to me.
Your horses stand by the door and wait for you.
Your bed is cold.
Now I cry, and the women cry with me.
Your fame is great, and my grief is great.

plan.english: Brother, where have you gone? Your horse came home alone. Your spear lies in the field. The wolves and the birds eat your flesh. I will go and seek your bones. I will gather them and burn them with fire. I will wash them with milk. I will put them under a stone and pour water and mead. Then you will go to our dead.

clauses.english: Brother, where have you gone?
Your horse came home alone.
Your spear lies in the field.
The wolves and the birds eat your flesh.
I will go and seek your bones.
I will gather them and burn them with fire.
I will wash them with milk.
I will put them under a stone and pour water and mead.
Then you will go to our dead.

title: Go Forth on the Old Paths

plan.english: Go forth, go forth on the old paths, by which our fathers went before. There you will find the Twin, king of the dead. Walk together with the old ones. Leave your suffering here, and come home. Take a new body. Do not turn back toward us. Do not be afraid of the darkness; Fire leads you. We remain here. May Earth, the mother, be dear to you.

clauses.english: Go forth, go forth on the old paths, by which our fathers went before.
There you will find the Twin, king of the dead.
Walk together with the old ones.
Leave your suffering here, and come home.
Take a new body.
Do not turn back toward us.
Do not be afraid of the darkness; Fire leads you.
We remain here.
May Earth, the mother, be dear to you.

plan.english: Go to this mother, Earth. Earth, receive this dead man. A mother covers her son with her garment; cover him. We have dug a hollow under the oak. We lay his bones into you. We have put this stone on him. This stone is the boundary of the dead. May the dead not cross it, and may death not come to us. May we live and see the sun.

clauses.english: Go to this mother, Earth.
Earth, receive this dead man.
A mother covers her son with her garment; cover him.
We have dug a hollow under the oak.
We lay his bones into you.
We have put this stone on him.
This stone is the boundary of the dead.
May the dead not cross it, and may death not come to us.
May we live and see the sun.

plan.english: Fathers, come to this feast! For you we have poured water, mead and milk. We have put meat on the grass. We light the fire on the hearth and call you with songs. Drink, eat, be satisfied! You who walked before, guard your grandsons. Do not be angry with us. Give us sons and cattle. Then go below.

clauses.english: Fathers, come to this feast!
For you we have poured water, mead and milk.
We have put meat on the grass.
We light the fire on the hearth and call you with songs.
Drink, eat, be satisfied!
You who walked before, guard your grandsons.
Do not be angry with us.
Give us sons and cattle.
Then go below.

plan.english: The path of the dead is long and dark. On it the sun does not grow bright. At the end of the path there is a bridge over a river. The good man crosses the bridge. The deceiving man falls below, and there he groans. For the good man the bridge is broad; for the deceiver it is narrow. On the other side a young woman meets the good one. She speaks: "I am your good mind and your good word." She leads him to the house of song.

clauses.english: The path of the dead is long and dark.
On it the sun does not grow bright.
At the end of the path there is a bridge over a river.
The good man crosses the bridge.
The deceiving man falls below, and there he groans.
For the good man the bridge is broad; for the deceiver it is narrow.
On the other side a young woman meets the good one.
She speaks: "I am your good mind and your good word."
She leads him to the house of song.

title: The Dead Friend in the Dream

plan.english: Bright-Fame was sleeping beside the boats. In a dream his dead friend came to him. He stood over his head and spoke: "You sleep, friend, and you have forgotten me. Burn me quickly with fire. Let me pass through the doors of the dead. The shades push me away. I walk alone by the river. Give me your hand; I shall not return." Bright-Fame stretched out his hands and seized nothing. The dead man vanished, and Bright-Fame woke up crying. Then he piled up timbers and burned the body of his friend.

clauses.english: Bright-Fame was sleeping beside the boats.
In a dream his dead friend came to him.
He stood over his head and spoke:
"You sleep, friend, and you have forgotten me.
Burn me quickly with fire.
Let me pass through the doors of the dead.
The shades push me away.
I walk alone by the river.
Give me your hand; I shall not return."
Bright-Fame stretched out his hands and seized nothing.
The dead man vanished, and Bright-Fame woke up crying.
Then he piled up timbers and burned the body of his friend.

title: At the Door of the Dead

plan.english: A dead man arrived at the house of the dead. At the door stood two old men. Their heads were white. They asked: "Who are you? Whose son are you?" "I am the offspring of Earth and Sky. I am thirsty; give me water. Do not give me the water of that river yonder. Whoever drinks it forgets his own lineage." They gave him a cup from the other river. Now he remembers his lineage. He entered among the heroes.

clauses.english: A dead man arrived at the house of the dead.
At the door stood two old men.
Their heads were white.
They asked: "Who are you?
Whose son are you?"
"I am the offspring of Earth and Sky.
I am thirsty; give me water.
Do not give me the water of that river yonder.
Whoever drinks it forgets his own lineage."
They gave him a cup from the other river.
Now he remembers his lineage.
He entered among the heroes.

plan.english: I am old, and my son lies below. The young lay the old to rest. I laid my son to rest. Why do I live, and he is dead? Death, why did you pass me by? His children call him, and he does not hear. I shall nourish them, my grandsons. I sit at the cold hearth and groan. When I am dead, they will put me beside him.

clauses.english: I am old, and my son lies below.
The young lay the old to rest.
I laid my son to rest.
Why do I live, and he is dead?
Death, why did you pass me by?
His children call him, and he does not hear.
I shall nourish them, my grandsons.
I sit at the cold hearth and groan.
When I am dead, they will put me beside him.

plan.english: Cattle die, brothers die, and you die. Whoever wins good fame, his fame is imperishable. What does not die? The fame of a dead man. Gold does not follow a mortal; his deeds follow him. Son, win good fame while you live.

clauses.english: Cattle die, brothers die, and you die.
Whoever wins good fame, his fame is imperishable.
What does not die?
The fame of a dead man.
Gold does not follow a mortal; his deeds follow him.
Son, win good fame while you live.

plan.english: Where do our dead dwell? They dwell in the third sky, with the Twin. There is light there, and joy. No one is hungry; no one is thirsty. They sit at the feast and drink mead. They hear the songs of their grandsons, and they rejoice. Honey and milk flow. When we are dead, we will go there.

clauses.english: Where do our dead dwell?
They dwell in the third sky, with the Twin.
There is light there, and joy.
No one is hungry; no one is thirsty.
They sit at the feast and drink mead.
They hear the songs of their grandsons, and they rejoice.
Honey and milk flow.
When we are dead, we will go there.

plan.english: New-Fame arrived among the dead and found his father, Kindly. Kindly asked him: "Son, why have you come here? You are young." "A spear struck me in battle, Kindly." "How is my house? Is my wife well?" "She is well, and she cries in the night." "Your grandson has grown strong; he leads your horses." "Then I rejoice. Sit down with me at the feast of the dead." Kindly gave him a cup of mead.

clauses.english: New-Fame arrived among the dead and found his father, Kindly.
Kindly asked him: "Son, why have you come here?
You are young."
"A spear struck me in battle, Kindly."
"How is my house?
Is my wife well?"
"She is well, and she cries in the night."
"Your grandson has grown strong; he leads your horses."
"Then I rejoice.
Sit down with me at the feast of the dead."
Kindly gave him a cup of mead.

title: A Father Tells His Son His Line

plan.english: Hear the race of your forebears. I am Man-Minded, son of Wolf-Fame. Wolf-Fame was born of Swift-Mind; he drove many cattle. Divine-Race begot Swift-Mind; Divine-Race slew the serpent. Divine-Race was born of a god, and his mother was a mortal woman. Divine-Race built a house on the hill, and we dwell in it. These are your race; remember them. Now I set a name on you, Good-Fame. When I am dead, pour water for me, and teach my deeds to your children.

clauses.english: Hear the race of your forebears.
I am Man-Minded, son of Wolf-Fame.
Wolf-Fame was born of Swift-Mind; he drove many cattle.
Divine-Race begot Swift-Mind; Divine-Race slew the serpent.
Divine-Race was born of a god, and his mother was a mortal woman.
Divine-Race built a house on the hill, and we dwell in it.
These are your race; remember them.
Now I set a name on you, Good-Fame.
When I am dead, pour water for me, and teach my deeds to your children.

plan.english: I am Bright-Horse, the great king, king of the peoples. I am the son of Good-Word and the grandson of Divine-Horses. Eight kings of our race were before me. A god gave me this land, and I rule it. I overpowered the enemies, and I gave gold to my men. To the gods I gave silver. Whoever breaks this stone, may the god strike him down, and may his line vanish. Whoever protects it, may many sons be born to him.

clauses.english: I am Bright-Horse, the great king, king of the peoples.
I am the son of Good-Word and the grandson of Divine-Horses.
Eight kings of our race were before me.
A god gave me this land, and I rule it.
I overpowered the enemies, and I gave gold to my men.
To the gods I gave silver.
Whoever breaks this stone, may the god strike him down, and may his line vanish.
Whoever protects it, may many sons be born to him.

title: The Sons of Sky and Earth

plan.english: Father Sky and Mother Earth begot two sons. The one was the Twin; the other was the first man. The Twin died; the man lived. He ploughed the field and sowed grain. He took a wife and begot children. From his children the peoples came forth. Mortals are the grandsons of the first man. When they are dead, they go to the brother of their forebear. He receives the dead in his house.

clauses.english: Father Sky and Mother Earth begot two sons.
The one was the Twin; the other was the first man.
The Twin died; the man lived.
He ploughed the field and sowed grain.
He took a wife and begot children.
From his children the peoples came forth.
Mortals are the grandsons of the first man.
When they are dead, they go to the brother of their forebear.
He receives the dead in his house.

plan.english: A son was born to the daughter of Bright-Fame. The daughter lifted the child and carried him to his grandfather. The women washed him and laid him on wool. The grandfather looked at him and said: "May he bear my name." Then they set the grandfather's name on the child. The grandfather gave him a white sheep. The grandson is Bright-Fame. "My name will not vanish; it lives in my grandson." May he grow and become a hero.

clauses.english: A son was born to the daughter of Bright-Fame.
The daughter lifted the child and carried him to his grandfather.
The women washed him and laid him on wool.
The grandfather looked at him and said: "May he bear my name."
Then they set the grandfather's name on the child.
The grandfather gave him a white sheep.
The grandson is Bright-Fame.
"My name will not vanish; it lives in my grandson."
May he grow and become a hero.

plan.english: The boy asked his maternal uncle: "Whose daughter is my mother?" "She is my sister; our father is New-Horses. New-Horses is the son of First-Fame, and First-Fame was a grandson of the River. The River bore a daughter, and from her came our race. The River is our mother; do not urinate into it. Pour mead into it for her."

clauses.english: The boy asked his maternal uncle: "Whose daughter is my mother?"
"She is my sister; our father is New-Horses.
New-Horses is the son of First-Fame, and First-Fame was a grandson of the River.
The River bore a daughter, and from her came our race.
The River is our mother; do not urinate into it.
Pour mead into it for her."

plan.english: The old man asked the boy: "How many forebears do you know?" "I know seven forebears: Bright-Mind, Kindly, First-Fame, Well-Born, Of-Famous-Race, Divine-Horses and Good-Path. The seventh was the son of a god." He said: "Whoever knows seven forebears, he is free. You are free." He rejoiced and gave the boy a knife of bronze.

clauses.english: The old man asked the boy: "How many forebears do you know?"
"I know seven forebears:
Bright-Mind, Kindly, First-Fame, Well-Born, Of-Famous-Race, Divine-Horses and Good-Path.
The seventh was the son of a god."
He said: "Whoever knows seven forebears, he is free.
You are free."
He rejoiced and gave the boy a knife of bronze.

title: The Races of Men Are Leaves

plan.english: A stranger asked Good-Path: "Whose son are you?" Good-Path spoke: "Why do you ask about my birth? The races of men are leaves. The wind pours the leaves down. In spring the tree brings forth new ones. A new race grows, and the old one vanishes. Hear my lineage. I am Good-Path, son of Bright-Mind, grandson of Swift-Horses." Then the stranger put his spear into the earth, and the two became friends.

clauses.english: A stranger asked Good-Path: "Whose son are you?"
Good-Path spoke: "Why do you ask about my birth?
The races of men are leaves.
The wind pours the leaves down.
In spring the tree brings forth new ones.
A new race grows, and the old one vanishes.
Hear my lineage.
I am Good-Path, son of Bright-Mind, grandson of Swift-Horses."
Then the stranger put his spear into the earth, and the two became friends.

plan.english: I am Good-Horses, daughter of Kindly, granddaughter of Divine-Race. My mother was Well-Born, the granddaughter of a king. My grandmother wove this garment from wool. The hands of the grandmother were swift. Its threads are red and white. Well-Born wore it, and now I wear it. When I am dead, my daughter will wear it, and my granddaughter after her. In this garment live the hands of our mothers.

clauses.english: I am Good-Horses, daughter of Kindly, granddaughter of Divine-Race.
My mother was Well-Born, the granddaughter of a king.
My grandmother wove this garment from wool.
The hands of the grandmother were swift.
Its threads are red and white.
Well-Born wore it, and now I wear it.
When I am dead, my daughter will wear it, and my granddaughter after her.
In this garment live the hands of our mothers.

title: The Lords Who Ruled and Died

plan.english: Hear the lords of our people, who ruled and went below. First-Fame ruled; he slew the serpent and freed the waters. Afterwards his son Swift-Mind ruled; he fell asleep in his house. Then the grandson of First-Fame, Wolf-Fame, ruled; he fell in war. No son was born to Wolf-Fame; his grandson ruled after him. He was Divine-Horses, and he ruled for many years. He became old and fell asleep in peace. Now his grandson rules us. May his fame be great and his line long.

clauses.english: Hear the lords of our people, who ruled and went below.
First-Fame ruled; he slew the serpent and freed the waters.
Afterwards his son Swift-Mind ruled; he fell asleep in his house.
Then the grandson of First-Fame, Wolf-Fame, ruled; he fell in war.
No son was born to Wolf-Fame; his grandson ruled after him.
He was Divine-Horses, and he ruled for many years.
He became old and fell asleep in peace.
Now his grandson rules us.
May his fame be great and his line long.

plan.english: Old Bright-Mind was lying on his bed, and he called his three sons. "I am going to the forebears. Divide the herd, and take each his own portion. Do not fight, brothers. In spring pour milk for me beside the stone. Set the names of the forebears on your offspring. Lay me on the hill, under the oak. So our line will not vanish." Then he fell asleep, and his breath went to the wind. The brothers lifted his body onto the wagon.

clauses.english: Old Bright-Mind was lying on his bed, and he called his three sons.
"I am going to the forebears.
Divide the herd, and take each his own portion.
Do not fight, brothers.
In spring pour milk for me beside the stone.
Set the names of the forebears on your offspring.
Lay me on the hill, under the oak.
So our line will not vanish."
Then he fell asleep, and his breath went to the wind.
The brothers lifted his body onto the wagon.

title: The Horses Born of the Wind

plan.english: The hero's horses were immortal; they were born of the wind. Their mother was eating grass beside a river; the wind came to her. She bore two swift horses. The gods gave them to him. When the hero fell, the horses cried. Their tears flowed to the earth. They did not eat, and they did not drink. Sky looked at them and said: "Why did we give you to a mortal? You are immortal; he was mortal."

plan.english: No son was born to Good-Word; his child was a daughter. Good-Word said: "Who will pour water for me when I am dead?" He gave his daughter to Swift-Mind and said: "Her boy will be my son." A boy was born to her; Good-Word lifted him and set a name on him. "You are my son and my grandson." So the line of Good-Word did not vanish.

title: The Father and the Son Between the Troops

plan.english: Two heroes came between the troops. The elder asked: "Who is your father?" The young one spoke: "My father is Of-Famous-Race. He went away and left me in the household as a child. He is dead; he will not return." The old man recognized him and said: "I am your father." The young one spoke: "You deceive me, old man." Then they threw spears. They fought, and the spear of Of-Famous-Race struck the young one. Of-Famous-Race cried: "I have slain my own son." So the line of Of-Famous-Race vanished.

The old man recognized him and said: "I am your father."

plan.english: Granddaughter, sit down beside me and hear the women of our line. Bright-Mind was a daughter of the River. She bore seven daughters and three sons. The youngest was Well-Born, my mother. I was born in winter, when snow lay on the fields. You are my granddaughter. We are the kin of Bright-Mind. Remember these women when offspring is born to you.

plan.english: Here lies my father, Swift-Horses. There lies his parent, Good-Minded, who slew many wolves. Under that great hill yonder lies the old man, Divine-Race. Their bones rest in the earth; their names live in my mouth. The wind moves the grass over them. For them I have poured out sweet mead on the stones. In spring I bring them grain and milk. My son will stand here and call on me.

plan.english: Good-Fame set up this stone for his parent, Kindly. Kindly fell in war, away from his home. He was the son of Man-Fame and the grandson of Good-Horses. His brothers and his wife cried. May the gods give him good things. This stone will stand, and his name will not vanish. Whoever passes by it, may he remember Kindly. Bright-Mind carved the words.

plan.english: My mother's father sang the fame of heroes. He taught the songs to my father. From him I learned them, and I sing them to my boy. The song goes from parent to son, and it does not perish. Mortals die; the song lives. In it the famous ones dwell. Imperishable fame! May my grandson sing it afterwards.
